content.text: Structured output for the lamplighter run. The kitchen's lights did not land in the built model, so `finished` is false.

input.summary:
Kitchen lighting measured and designed: designer's layout plus one hanging lantern at (49,9,62) gives min 8, 0 dark, 0 dim on a scratch copy (checked with mcd room). Added that lantern at the end of parts/room-12.mjs build(g).
Not landed: shell.mjs carves the kitchen box to air, runParts counts that air as placed and refuses the lantern (placed 0, refused 1), so the built kitchen is still 57 dark cells and 68 dim.
make.sh wrote a whole build.nbt, but the lighting is not in it, so this part is not finished.
left: Kitchen is dark in build.nbt: 57 dark and 68 dim cells, because no furniture and no lamp can land there. parts/shell.mjs box(37,61,58,75) fills the interior with air, and runParts locks every air cell an earlier part placed.

The lock is systemic, not kitchen-only: all 36 room parts report placed 0 in parts-report.json. Only shell-owned parts plus galleries, porch and outbuildings place anything. The shell owner must stop claiming room interior air, or runParts must let room parts write into shell-carved air. Either fix is outside lamplighter scope.

The designer's restore block in room-12.mjs (furniture and lanterns) is still commented out, so the kitchen layout has never been tested in the real build. On the scratch copy the designer's layout alone is OK (min 7, one dim cell at x51 z62); the lamp added at (49,9,62) takes it to min 8. Once the lock is lifted, the designer should restore the layout and the lantern will land, with the counter-top lanterns at y5 resting on the counters.
parts/room-12.mjs edits: B added to the import, and one line at the end of build(g): g.set(49, 9, 62, ...B.lantern(true)). It is refused until the lock lifts; the refusal shows in parts-report.json.

Outside the kitchen, mcd check on the build reports structure problems that are not mine: floating groups in the gazebo area near 9..17,2..14,77..85, lanterns floating at 79,5,68 / 79,5,72 / 84,5,67, and an unsupported white_carpet at 41,4,78. Left for the owners.

waste.what: Dry-running the designer's kitchen layout: I copied its restore arrays into a /tmp script, saved a scratch .nbt, and measured it with mcd room. Two retries came from zsh not word-splitting $var, which passed bad coordinates into the lantern test.
waste.cost: about 4 scratch scripts and 3 failed shell runs
waste.tool: mcd room --layout <room-module> (apply the module's restore block or its layers() calls onto a copy of build.nbt, skipping the runParts lock, then print the room report). Also mcd room --add x,y,z,block for a single candidate lamp.

waste.what: Finding out why the kitchen's writes were refused: I read shell.mjs box() and runParts' lock rules and wrote a probe that runs the shell plus a lantern write, to see which part owns each refused cell.
waste.cost: one library read, one probe script, one make.sh run
waste.tool: runParts should name the earlier part and the box that locks each refused cell (for example: refused: 49,9,62 locked by 'mansion shell' air at box 37,61,58,75). mcd room could print the same lock line when the walk or light says dark.

waste.what: Working out which kitchen cells are dark and which lamp spots clear them: I took the light map from mcd light and the lantern spot from the room report, then tested candidates one by one.
waste.cost: 2 candidate builds, each a full copy and a room run
waste.tool: mcd room already suggests the lamp spot; a --try option that tests the top suggestion and prints the new min/dark counts would save the candidate runs.

companions.task: Owner of the mansion shell (parts/shell.mjs): stop filling the kitchen box, and the other room boxes, with air, or leave those cells unwritten, so room furniture and lamps can land. Then the designer can restore the kitchen layout.
Place the designer's kitchen fittings (counters, smoker, furnace, sink, barrels, island) once the room is unlocked, so the counter-top lanterns at y5 have something to stand on.
